objective: Implement a non-mutating, traceable missing-data and feature-eligibility diagnostic layer without changing the frozen scientific baseline or inventing measurements.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Project baseline v0.2.0 must preserve the 42-feature schema, model artifact, class order, and historical cutoff.

CPVS issue #170 remains unresolved: 781602 parent objects, 741786 reconstructed candidates, 730184 published reference members, 11602 candidate-only, and zero published-only on the pinned finite-SNR run.

The native feature pipeline filters invalid observations, uses 10-observation and 30-observation eligibility thresholds for basic and Lomb–Scargle features, and intentionally returns NaN for ineligible features.
Cross-band color can be defined from one valid observation per band, while a sample-standard-deviation variability ratio requires at least two observations.
The first CI run on this PR found lint-only issues in the new diagnostic helper; those were corrected in commit f40ed855f1b64005696fd210a03fb3b52bb9fb45.

baseline.scope: Feature eligibility diagnostics only; no feature values, model artifacts, thresholds, training data, class order, or CPVS selection rules changed.

change.rationale: Report why a feature is unavailable without fabricating source measurements, imputing in the extraction layer, or rejecting an entire object when only one analysis is ineligible.

expected_improvement: Expose raw and valid observation counts by band and the current feature-group eligibility thresholds.
Differentiate mathematically undefined sample-standard-deviation ratios from unavailable cross-band colors.
Provide regression tests for missingness reasons, invalid-row filtering, JSON serialization, input immutability, and missing schema columns.
Preserve the frozen v0.2.0 feature vector and keep exact CPVS membership reproduction as a separate gate.
Honor the same optional historical cutoff as the canonical feature pipeline so diagnostics do not misattribute missing features when post-cutoff observations exist.

reproducibility.before: Non-finite feature values could be emitted without a structured per-feature eligibility reason.
reproducibility.after: An opt-in JSON-safe diagnostic report records per-band counts, thresholds, conservative non-finite reasons, and cutoff-aware eligibility.

reliability.before: A one-observation band could yield an undefined ddof=1 variability ratio with no explicit explanation.
reliability.after: The diagnostic reports that sample standard deviation requires at least two observations without altering the feature value.

findings: Missing measurement, unavailable derived feature, and invalid astronomical object are distinct states.

A derived estimate from raw observations must not be silently substituted for a catalog's fit-derived value; any alternative estimator needs a distinct definition, quality policy, uncertainty, provenance, and validation.
A successful schema/order check is not proof that every feature is numerically computable.
The diagnostic helper is opt-in; integration into every API/UI response remains a separate compatibility-reviewed task.
This change does not resolve the CPVS published-membership discrepancy or establish full scientific model validity.

open_blockers: The helper remains opt-in until API/UI integration is separately designed and compatibility-tested.
CPVS exact membership remains an independent unresolved scientific validation blocker.
Callers must pass the same cutoff_mjd used to generate the supplied feature mapping.

knowledge_carried_forward: Eligibility counts and reasons must use the same historical cutoff as the feature vector being diagnosed.
Do not impute or fabricate measurements in the feature-extraction layer.
Do not alter the frozen v0.2.0 model, feature order, or CPVS selection predicate in this PR.
Do not merge before all current-head CI jobs pass.
Keep product missing-data policy and historical CPVS membership reproduction as separate workstreams.
